title: KV Cache Compression, But What Must We Give in Return?
one_line_claim: Comprehensive empirical benchmark revealing that different KV cache compression methods (quantization, token dropping, linear-time models, prompt compression) have fundamentally different reliability profiles across task categories, with prefill compression being critical but risky.
method_summary: Benchmarks 10 KV cache compression methods across 16 long-context tasks spanning 7 categories (single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic, code completion, needle-in-haystack). Each method is evaluated on both prefill and decode stages. Results report accuracy/F1 normalized against uncompressed baseline.

key_findings.finding: Prefill-stage compression is critical for performance but introduces high variability in method reliability.
key_findings.quote: Prefill compression is critical for methods' overall performance. However, directly compressing prefills often introduces risk.

key_findings.finding: Quantization methods achieve consistent performance across diverse task types; token dropping methods excel on specific tasks but show high variance.
key_findings.quote: quantization methods are fairly reliable across all categories. However, token dropping sometimes excels on specific tasks but sometimes severely underperforms.

key_findings.finding: Needle-in-a-haystack retrieval remains a fundamental challenge for all compression methods.
key_findings.quote: Needle-in-a-haystack remains challenging for all methods, with even the best-performing methods showing degradation.

limitations: Benchmark covers long-context generation but does not deeply analyze computational cost/latency tradeoffs.
Focuses on task-level accuracy metrics without per-token quality analysis.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both measure degradation of LLM quality under KV cache compression and examine which aspects of the cache are critical for maintaining generation quality.
differs_on: This paper measures post-hoc task accuracy across diverse benchmarks; HERALD predicts failure onset during generation from real-time logit features, enabling pre-failure intervention.
This paper compares compression methods at a high level; HERALD operates at per-token granularity to detect the exact moment compression causes failure.
This paper focuses on which compression methods work for which task types; HERALD focuses on detecting when any compression method is about to cause catastrophic failure.
